subject: research/decision-regret-transfer
professional: a learning theorist who reviews surrogate-regret / calibration-function papers (COLT, JMLR). They would check first that the average-case certificate psi^{-1}(E[D]) is a valid upper bound, i.e. that the computed psi really lies below delta everywhere (Jensen needs psi <= delta), then whether the binary result is already known (Reid & Williamson 2009/2011 surrogate regret bounds for proper losses; Steinwart 2007 calibration functions), then the abstain/audit extension against the classification-with-reject literature

evidence.correctness: The exact calibration function delta is right: independent numpy/scipy recomputation (rel_entr KL, own region logic, 4001^2 numpy brute force) reproduces E1 to 6 digits (e.g. tau=0.02 eps=0.05 log 0.038991), E4 within brute-force grid error (c=0.1 log 0.04440 vs grid 0.04468, grid can only overestimate), E2 log bounds 0.0706/0.0584/0.0432/0.0226 and 0.0129 vs reported 0.0128 (shipped 0.012846: chord error), E5 S and regret within Monte Carlo error with a different RNG (noisy brier 0.0086/0.0077, log 0.0220). But the headline deliverable, the average-case certificate psi^{-1}(E[D]), is not a valid bound: envelope() (model.py:115) takes the lower convex hull of delta sampled on a 400-point grid, which for a convex delta is the piecewise-linear chord ABOVE delta between nodes, so psi >= delta there and Jensen fails. A point-mass verifier at a tight pair violates the certificate: Costs(1,1,c=0.2), Brier, eps=0.001: E[D]=1e-6, realised regret 0.001, certificate 0.0004 (2.5x); scanning eps from 1e-4 the worst ratio is 25x for both rules. The very pair E6 uses to show the certificate is 'attained' (tau=0.1, eta=0.15, q=0.1) gives regret 0.050000 against certificate 0.049993. Realistic smooth verifiers (sigma 0.01-0.1) do not violate it, so E5's 'never violated' is true but not a guarantee.
evidence.completeness: README promises: 7 tests (Ran 7 tests in 5.9 s, OK), run.py reproduces results.txt (rerun in a scratch copy, byte-identical, 6.9 s), figure regenerated from results.txt (byte-identical SVG), whitepaper with R1-R5, live page https://marisstella.app/research/decision-regret-transfer/ (HTTP 200, '7 tests', findings text, figure at .../regret_bound.svg 200 image/svg+xml). Every claimed artefact exists and runs end to end. README:10 says run.py takes '~1 min'; it takes 7 s.
evidence.verification: `cd research/decision-regret-transfer && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 7 OK in 5.9 s. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py, 5 SURVIVED: audit/reject boundary 1-c/R -> 1-c/A (every audit test uses A=R), the audit-optimality cutoff A*R/(A+R) -> min(A,R)/2, max_regret evaluated at eta 0.9 instead of 1, regret_bound flat-segment branch x1 -> x0, and multiplying every envelope point by 1.5 (a 1.5x too-optimistic certificate). Only swapping the region edge in delta() was caught (4 failures). The last survivor exposes a test written in the wrong direction: test_envelope_is_convex_and_below_delta (tests/test_model.py:57) asserts regret_bound(h, delta(eps)) <= eps + 1e-2, but psi <= delta means regret_bound(h, delta(eps)) >= eps; the test can only catch a too-conservative envelope, never the unsound one. Nothing pins results.txt.
evidence.craft: Read model.py (159 lines), __init__.py, tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, figure.py. Compact stdlib code with a docstring that states the math. Defects: wildcard `from .model import *` with no __all__ (exports math, EPS); Costs.action returns None for q outside [0,1] and cost() then KeyErrors on None; delta_bruteforce is O(n^2) pure Python; envelope sampling has no lower-bound correction although the module docstring calls the result exact; test name test_bound_holds_and_is_tight checks no tightness; test comment 'with equality reachable' for the hinge is wrong (ratio is 1+|f|, infimum not attained, E3 prints 1.0100); figure.py carries an unused generic table() parser; run.py inserts src into sys.path.
evidence.claims: Backed by files: E1 closed forms, E2 values (0.071 -> 0.013), E4 audit tightening, E5 '8-26%' (0.08-0.26) and 'never violated in simulation', R1 9-digit match (test places=9). Not backed: (1) the page and research/README.md:65 call the output a 'certified cap', and the whitepaper (whitepaper.md:20, Implication 1 at :43) an 'auditable cap', but the grid envelope under-certifies by up to 25x at small gaps; (2) README:14 and whitepaper.md:40 'attained by a two-point verifier' / 'exactly attained': E6 only shows delta is attained pointwise, and the shipped certificate at that pair is 0.049993 < realised 0.05, i.e. violated, not attained; (3) whitepaper.md:44 Implication 2 'log score is preferable when fault cost >> slashing cost' contradicts its own R2 caveat (whitepaper.md:29: different units, 'compares each rule's own guarantee, not the rules'); (4) README:10 '~1 min' vs 7 s measured. 'Stylised' disclaimer present; Limits section mentions grid error but not that the error is in the unsafe direction.
evidence.fitness: Job: a protocol researcher wants to turn a verifier's measured excess score into a cap on decision loss for given (A, R, c). They can call delta() and trust it (it recomputes), but cannot trust regret_bound(envelope(...)) as a certificate without the lower-step fix, and the binary closed forms are textbook: Reid & Williamson (ICML 2009 'Surrogate regret bounds for proper losses'; JMLR 2011) give exactly the tight cost-weighted regret bound of a proper loss as its Bregman divergence at the threshold, and Steinwart (2007) the calibration-function machinery; the audit band is the classification-with-reject setting (Chow 1970; Bartlett & Wegkamp 2008; Ramaswamy, Tewari & Agarwal 2018 on abstain-consistent surrogates). None of these is cited; the README does not claim novelty, but nothing says what is new. What is plausibly new is the three-action exact delta for log and Brier with the audit band; that part is sound. Not part of a programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md.
evidence.domain: Against the standard calibration-function / surrogate-regret method (Bartlett, Jordan & McAuliffe 2006; Steinwart 2007; Reid & Williamson 2009): delta defined correctly as an infimum over pairs, the inner minimisation at the region edge is right for Bregman divergences (monotone in |eta-q|), and Jensen through the convex envelope is the textbook route. It departs in the one place a reviewer checks first: the convex envelope must lower-bound delta, and a hull of point samples of a nondecreasing function does not; the standard fix is to hull the lower step corners (k*h, delta((k-1)*h)), which I verified in a scratch copy gives 0 violations over 3,000 tight pairs on four configurations and loosens the s=0.01 log bound by about 2-4%. Uses one-component Brier (eta-q)^2 without saying so (the two-component convention doubles D). Missing citations above.

defects.what: The average-case certificate is unsound: envelope() hulls point samples of a convex delta, so between grid nodes psi lies ABOVE delta and Jensen fails. A point-mass verifier at a tight pair beats the 'certified cap' by up to 25x at small score gaps (Costs(1,1,c=0.2), Brier, E[D]=1e-6: regret 0.001, certificate 0.0004), and the E6 pair itself gives regret 0.050000 > certificate 0.049993. Fix: hull (k h, delta((k-1) h)) instead (delta is nondecreasing), verified 0 violations

test_envelope_is_convex_and_below_delta asserts regret_bound(h, delta(eps)) <= eps + 1e-2, the opposite of psi <= delta; it can never catch an unsound envelope (a 1.5x inflated envelope passes). 5 of 6 seeded mutants survive: every audit test uses A=R so the 1-c/R edge and the audit cutoff are unpinned; nothing pins results.txt

'certified cap' (page, research/README.md:65), 'auditable cap' (whitepaper Implication 1) and 'attained by a two-point verifier' (README:14, whitepaper.md:40) are not backed: the shipped certificate is violated at small gaps and at the E6 pair; E6 only shows delta, not psi^{-1}, is attained
Implication 2 'log score is preferable when fault cost >> slashing cost' contradicts R2's own caveat that the nats-vs-squared-error certificates compare each rule's guarantee, not the rules

The binary result (tight regret bound of a proper loss for cost-weighted decisions = its Bregman divergence at the threshold) is Reid & Williamson (ICML 2009; JMLR 2011); Steinwart 2007 (calibration functions) and the classification-with-reject literature (Chow 1970; Bartlett & Wegkamp 2008; Ramaswamy, Tewari & Agarwal 2018) cover the audit band; none is cited and nothing states what is new
README says run.py takes '~1 min'; measured 6.9 s
Wildcard export with no __all__; Costs.action returns None for q outside [0,1], then cost() raises KeyError(None); test comment claims hinge equality is reachable (ratio is 1+|f|, infimum only)

verdict: A tidy, reproducible note whose exact calibration function is right and whose headline certificate is not. delta recomputes independently (E1 to 6 digits with scipy KL, E4 against a 4001^2 numpy brute force, E5 with a separate RNG), and run.py and figure.py reproduce their committed outputs byte for byte. But psi^{-1}(E[D]), sold as a 'certified cap', is built from a convex hull of grid samples that lies above delta between nodes, so a point-mass verifier beats it by up to 25x at small gaps and the E6 'attained' pair violates it (0.050000 vs 0.049993); the test meant to guard this asserts the wrong inequality, and 5 of 6 seeded mutants survive. The binary result is Reid & Williamson (2009) uncited, and Implication 2 contradicts the paper's own caveat. A one-line lower-step envelope fixes the soundness.
